trailhead.name: Depot Creek Road parking (Chilliwack Lake Road, BC), then walk the old road to the border at Monument 65

identifiedBy.fact: Easy Mox NE Ridge party parked at a small lot at a fork on Depot Creek Road near milepost 1.5 (about 2,350 ft), walked old road about 2 miles to the border, then Ouzel Lake and Redoubt Glacier to the NE ridge

otherFacts.value: Chilliwack Lake Road, left before the yellow bridge near north end of Chilliwack Lake, then about 1.5 mi on Depot Creek Road
headwall 2 pitches class 5, then about 0.5 mi class 3-4 crest, pinnacles, class 5 pitch to notch, final class 3-4 pitch
two single-rope rappels to ledge, then double-rope rappel to glacier
NPS backcountry registration kiosk just past border swath

notes: Strong for the start (page is this exact route, NE Ridge of Easy Mox, and agrees with the sibling's Depot Creek Road Trailhead). No coordinate on any page; official candidates are only BC points 17+ km off and none is Depot Creek. SummitPost, Mountaineers 403.

trailhead.name: Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center

identifiedBy.fact: Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center

notes: Named by the route text only; not re-verified on a page. No land-manager coordinate found. Search showed aggregator points (Waze 44.18283,-73.96395; Roadtrippers 44.2115,-73.9541) about 3 km apart, not usable. Leave to OSM name match.

otherFacts.value: East Ridge class 2 (Burd), from Amphitheater Lake
class 2 via Dumbbell Lakes

notes: Two real starts with one report each: Bob Burd started at South Lake (Bishop Pass, Dusy Basin, Knapsack Pass, Palisade Creek, Cataract Creek, Amphitheater Lake, East Ridge); earlier pass found climber.org 2007/1718 from Taboose Pass. A search summary says SummitPost calls Bishop Pass the common access, but SummitPost returned 403 so that is unverified. Wikipedia has no access info. If forced: South Lake (USFS 37.169305,-118.565813) slightly stronger than Taboose, still weak.

identifiedBy.fact: LeConte Glacier / Old Guard trips start at Cascade Pass Trailhead at the end of Cascade River Road, then Cascade Pass and Cache Col; route text also names Cascade River Road

summitEvidence.fact: Overview calls it a short roped alternative to the standard scramble, 2-3 pitches up Old Guard's east side from LeConte Glacier; never says it tops out

otherFacts.value: NW snowfinger then class 3 gabbro scramble, summit about 8240 ft
gate locked 2 mi short of Cascade River road end in 2020 (extra 2 mi, about 1000 ft walk)

notes: Moderate: pages open describe the NW side of Old Guard from the same LeConte Glacier, all starting at Cascade Pass; no page opened describes the east route itself (SummitPost 403, search summary only). Cascade Pass to Cache Col is the standard way onto LeConte Glacier; Suiattle/Downey Creek alternative is closed per route text.

trailhead.name: Sigurd Creek Trailhead (Ashlu Creek Road, spur A-200)

identifiedBy.fact: 2013 VOC Ossa Mountain trip: Sigurd Creek trailhead via Ashlu Creek road, branch A-200 about 2.3 km past the bridges, park on the right just past the fork

otherFacts.value: Highway 99 to Squamish Valley Road, left onto Ashlu Creek road, bridge over Squamish River
about 15-20 km, 1500 m gain to lake camp (planned)
1960-07-25 east ridge (Chambers, Bryan, Rode) per Wikipedia via search summary

notes: Moderate, weak on the ridge: the VOC page does not say east or west ridge, and other sources call the west ridge the usual line via Sigurd Creek. Sigurd Creek is the only road-access trailhead found for Ossa. Stored text says 30 min from Squamish, consistent. No coordinate; Song page body unreadable via WebFetch.

identifiedBy.fact: North-side route: snow finger in the north gully from Overcoat Glacier, descent east gully with two rappels; trip started at Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead (gated, bike about 7 mi to Hardscrabble Horse Camp)

otherFacts.value: helmet, ice tools, crampons, 60 m rope, bike
east gully, downclimb dihedral, two full-length rappels to glacier
rocks above Overcoat Glacier, about 6600 ft

notes: Moderate. Replaces the earlier Dingford guess: that is the Mountaineers' listed start (Dingford Creek TH, FR 5620, 26 mi, via search summary, page 403) and the route is the same long approach, but the opened trip report on the north side names Dutch Miller Gap TH. Both sit on the same road system; two starts, so keep the note. Dingford is USFS 47.517325,-121.4543 if the owner prefers the official lot. No coordinate for Dutch Miller Gap TH found.

identifiedBy.fact: Route named Indian Wells Canyon; old road to a wilderness barricade then canyon trail, about 7 mi round trip

otherFacts.value: end of Indian Wells Canyon Road, high clearance advised, trailhead about 5390-5640 ft (search summary, not opened)
Owens Creek canyon trail to about 7800 ft, then ridge, use trail to summit (climber.org 2006/1471, a different canyon trailhead OPPARK)

notes: Name-level only; the opened climber.org report uses a different trailhead (Owens Creek, 7.2 mi up SE164), so it does not confirm this one. No coordinate.

identifiedBy.fact: Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb; Bradley Pond Trail and Panther Brook herd path

notes: Named by route text. Aggregator coordinates seen (AllTrails 44.08649,-74.05598; a hiking blog 44.08682,-74.05599; Santanoni Range trailhead 44.06907,-74.06149 is a separate lot on Upper Works Road, the Bradley Pond trail start is likely that one but unverified). No land-manager coordinate.

otherFacts.value: about 10 mi via Glen Aulin to Return Creek, then 4500 ft gain, 18 hr round trip

notes: Burd's Tuolumne Meadows trip (Glen Aulin trail) is presented as unusually hard; the same page says a companion day-hiked Pettit and Volunteer from Virginia Lakes, the more common approach (north side). Two starts, nothing ties this route to one. SummitPost 403.
